answers.value: Only statements 2 and 4 are correct - the State cannot contract Aadhaar data out to private corporations, and Aadhaar can be required for benefits funded from the Consolidated Fund of India
answers.reasoning: In K.S. Puttaswamy (2018) the Supreme Court read down the authentication-data retention rule to six months, not the three months stated, so statement 1 is wrong. Statement 2 follows from the striking down of Section 57 of the Aadhaar Act, which had allowed body corporates and private persons to use Aadhaar for identification; the State can no longer share Aadhaar data with private companies by contract. Statement 3 is wrong for the same reason - the Court held Aadhaar was not mandatory for bank accounts, mobile connections, school admissions or insurance. Statement 4 is the one use the Court expressly upheld: Section 7 permits Aadhaar to be required for subsidies, benefits and services charged to the Consolidated Fund of India.

answers.value: The Rajya Sabha has powers equal to the Lok Sabha in amending the Constitution
answers.reasoning: Article 368 requires a constitutional amendment Bill to be passed separately by each House by the prescribed special majority, and there is no provision for a joint sitting to resolve a deadlock - so on amendment the two Houses are exactly equal. Creating a new All India Service is not an equal power but a special power of the Rajya Sabha alone, since Article 312 requires its resolution to start the process. Removing the government by a no-confidence motion, and voting demands for grants (and therefore moving cut motions on them), lie exclusively with the Lok Sabha.

answers.value: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct; MPLADS funds are non-lapsable, so statement 3 is wrong
answers.reasoning: The MPLADS guidelines require the funds to be spent on works creating durable community assets - drinking water, education, public health, sanitation, roads - so statement 1 holds. They also earmark 15 per cent of a member's allocation for areas with Scheduled Caste population and 7.5 per cent for Scheduled Tribe areas, so statement 2 holds. Statement 3 is wrong and is what eliminates option C: MPLADS funds are expressly non-lapsable and an unspent balance is carried forward to the next year. The guidelines further require the District Authority to inspect at least 10 per cent of the works under implementation every year, so statement 4 holds.

answers.value: Protection against untouchability falls under the Right to Equality
answers.reasoning: Untouchability is abolished and its practice in any form forbidden by Article 17, which sits within Articles 14 to 18 - the group of rights headed Right to Equality. The Right against Exploitation is the nearest distractor but covers different ground: Articles 23 and 24 deal with traffic in human beings, begar and forced labour, and the employment of children in hazardous work.

answers.value: Separation of the judiciary from the executive is enjoined by a Directive Principle of State Policy (Article 50)
answers.reasoning: Article 50, in Part IV, directs the State to take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State. The Preamble contains no such direction, the Seventh Schedule only distributes legislative subjects between the Union and the States, and the separation is a written constitutional mandate rather than a mere convention.

answers.value: The Macro Economic Framework Statement is mandated by the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003
answers.reasoning: Section 3 of the FRBM Act, 2003 obliges the Central Government to lay before both Houses, along with the Budget, the Macro-Economic Framework Statement, the Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement and the Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement. It is therefore a statutory requirement, not a convention. Article 112 deals with the Annual Financial Statement and Article 110(1) defines a Money Bill; Article 113 deals with demands for grants - none of them mentions these statements.

answers.value: A constitutional government is by definition a limited government
answers.reasoning: Constitutionalism means government bound by a higher law: the Constitution both confers and confines the powers of every organ of the State, so that power is exercised within defined limits and subject to checks. A government may be popular, multi-party, or dominated by its legislature and still be arbitrary; what makes it constitutional is precisely that its authority is limited.

answers.value: The Preamble, the Directive Principles and the Fundamental Duties all reflect the Universal Declaration of Human Rights
answers.reasoning: The Preamble's promise of justice, liberty, equality, fraternity and the dignity of the individual restates the opening ideals of the UDHR. The Directive Principles carry its economic, social and cultural rights - the right to work, to a living wage, to education, to public assistance and to health - which the Fundamental Rights do not cover. The Fundamental Duties answer to Article 29(1) of the UDHR, which declares that everyone has duties to the community; that link is the judgement call in the item, since the Duties were inserted in 1976 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, but the parallel with Article 29 is a real one, and only option D includes all three.

answers.value: Statements 1 and 2 are correct - free legal aid on the ground of income turns on being below the prescribed ceiling, and not all senior citizens qualify
answers.reasoning: Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 gives free legal services to listed classes - members of Scheduled Castes and Tribes, women and children, persons with disabilities, industrial workmen, persons in custody, victims of trafficking or of mass disaster - and otherwise to any person whose annual income is below the prescribed ceiling, which NALSA generally puts at Rs 1,00,000, so statement 1 stands. Statement 4 is wrong because age by itself confers no entitlement: a senior citizen must still satisfy one of the statutory grounds, and the statement is unconditional. Statement 3 is wrong because Other Backward Classes are not a listed class and no Rs 3,00,000 ceiling applies to them. Statement 2 is the weak link and is accepted here largely because the other two fail; the income ceilings are in any case set by the State Governments and vary, so no single national figure is beyond argument. Option C is the runner-up.

answers.value: Only pairs 1 and 3 are correctly matched - Alma-Ata with healthcare and Talanoa Dialogue with climate change
answers.reasoning: The Alma-Ata Declaration of 1978 proclaimed Health for All through primary health care, so pair 1 is right; the Talanoa Dialogue was the facilitative dialogue launched at COP23 under the UNFCCC to take stock of collective climate action, so pair 3 is right. The Hague Conventions of 1899 and 1907 codified the laws and customs of war - biological and chemical weapons are governed by the Biological Weapons Convention of 1972 and the Chemical Weapons Convention of 1993 - so pair 2 is wrong. The Under2 Coalition is the Under 2 Degrees group of states and regions pledging deep emission cuts; it has nothing to do with child rights, so pair 4 is wrong.

answers.value: In a parliamentary system the Government is responsible to Parliament and can be removed by it
answers.reasoning: The defining feature of a parliamentary executive is the collective responsibility of the council of ministers to the legislature: the government holds office only so long as it commands the confidence of the popular House and falls when that confidence is withdrawn. Option A describes a national or all-party government, option C describes a directly elected executive answerable to the voters, and option D describes a fixed-term presidential-style executive that Parliament cannot dismiss.

answers.value: The Directive Principles of State Policy declare the ideal of a Welfare State
answers.reasoning: The welfare-state programme is spelt out in Part IV: Article 38 requires the State to secure a social order in which justice informs all institutions of national life, Article 39 speaks of adequate means of livelihood and the distribution of material resources for the common good, and Articles 41 to 43 promise work, education, public assistance and a living wage. The Preamble sets out ideals without prescribing this programme, and the Fundamental Rights operate mainly as restraints on State action rather than as positive obligations of welfare.

answers.value: Only statement 2 is correct - judicial review is provided for, but the Constitution nowhere defines a 'basic structure'
answers.reasoning: The expression basic structure appears nowhere in the Constitution. It is a doctrine evolved by the Supreme Court in Kesavananda Bharati (1973) and filled out case by case since, which is why the Court has never given an exhaustive list of its contents - so statement 1 is wrong. Judicial review, by contrast, is expressly provided for: Article 13 makes laws inconsistent with the Fundamental Rights void, and Articles 32 and 226 arm the Supreme Court and the High Courts to enforce them, so statement 2 is correct. [Answer corrected to D from the official UPSC answer key; an independent blind derivation had reached B. The reasoning above argues for B and is retained so the disagreement is visible rather than hidden.]

answers.value: Gandhism and Marxism agree on the final goal of a stateless society
answers.reasoning: Both look forward to a society in which the coercive state has disappeared: Marx to the withering away of the state once the classless society is reached, Gandhi to an enlightened anarchy of self-governing village republics in which the individual is his own ruler. They part company on everything else - Gandhi rejected class struggle in favour of trusteeship and class harmony, opposed the forcible abolition of private property, and denied that economic forces determine the course of history.

answers.value: The bureaucracy is an agency for the implementation of public policy
answers.reasoning: The civil service is the permanent executive: policy is framed by the political executive and the legislature, and the bureaucracy's defining function is to carry it out. The other three describe consequences to which bureaucratic action may contribute but which do not define the institution - widening democracy, strengthening federalism and securing political stability are the work of representative and constitutional institutions, not of the civil service as such.

answers.value: The Preamble is a part of the Constitution but has no legal effect independently of the other parts
answers.reasoning: In Kesavananda Bharati (1973) the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution, overruling the contrary view taken in the Berubari Union reference. But it is neither a source of power nor a source of prohibition, and it is not enforceable in a court by itself; its use is to resolve ambiguity in the provisions that follow. That is exactly the position option D states. Option C overstates it by putting the Preamble on a par with the enforceable articles, and options A and B understate it.

answers.value: Gold Tranche (Reserve Tranche) is a credit facility granted by the IMF to its members
answers.reasoning: A member pays part of its IMF quota in foreign currency or SDRs rather than in its own currency, and that portion is the reserve tranche, historically the gold tranche. The member may draw up to it automatically and without conditionality, because in substance it is drawing on its own reserves held with the Fund. It is not a World Bank lending window, has nothing to do with the WTO, and is not an operation of a domestic central bank.

answers.value: Statements 2 and 3 are correct - the Directive Principles are not enforceable by any court but are to guide the State in making laws
answers.reasoning: Article 37 says the provisions of Part IV shall not be enforceable by any court, but that they are nevertheless fundamental in the governance of the country and it shall be the duty of the State to apply them in making laws. Statement 2 is a direct restatement of the first half of that Article and statement 3 of the second half, so both are correct. Statement 1 asserts the exact opposite of statement 2 and is therefore wrong.

answers.value: Only statement 1 is correct - a non-member may be a Minister for six months, but conviction does not bring a permanent electoral disqualification
answers.reasoning: Article 164(4) allows a person who is not a member of the State Legislature to hold ministerial office, but only for six consecutive months, after which he ceases to be a Minister unless he is elected in the meantime - which is the substance of statement 1. Statement 2 is clearly wrong: Section 8(3) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 disqualifies a convicted person from the date of conviction and for a further six years from release, a fixed period and not a permanent bar. Note that statement 1 is loosely worded - being eligible to vote (18 years) is not by itself sufficient, because Article 173 requires a person to be at least 25 to be a member of a Legislative Assembly and the courts have held a Minister must be qualified for membership. On that strict reading of the words as printed the answer would be D, and that is the runner-up here; the answer given takes the phrase as identifying an ordinary citizen rather than as stating the qualifying condition. [Answer corrected to D from the official UPSC answer key; an independent blind derivation had reached A. The reasoning above argues for A and is retained so the disagreement is visible rather than hidden.]

answers.value: Statements 1 and 3 are correct - the President may summon Parliament at any place, and no minimum number of sitting days is prescribed
answers.reasoning: Article 85(1) empowers the President to summon each House to meet at such time and place as he thinks fit, so statement 1 is correct. The same Article prescribes only that six months shall not intervene between the last sitting of one session and the first sitting of the next; it lays down no number of sessions and no minimum number of sitting days. The three sessions held each year - Budget, Monsoon and Winter - are a matter of convention, not of constitutional provision, so statement 2 is wrong and statement 3 is right.

answers.value: Only pairs 2 and 3 are correctly matched - Banian as the Company's Indian agent and Mirasidar as the designated revenue payer
answers.reasoning: A banian was the Indian broker, agent and money-lender attached to a European trading house or to a servant of the East India Company, so pair 2 is right. Mirasidars were the hereditary landholders of the Tamil country who held mirasi right in the village and were the recognised payers of revenue to the State, so pair 3 is right. An aurang was not an officer at all but a place - the warehouse or depot at which the Company's textiles were collected from the weavers before shipment - so pairing it with charge of the treasury is wrong.

answers.value: Statements 2 and 3 are correct - the Lokottaravadins branched from the Mahasanghikas, whose deification of the Buddha fed Mahayana; the Sthaviravadins are not Mahayana
answers.reasoning: The great schism divided the sangha into the Sthaviravadins, the Elders, from whom the Theravada line descends, and the Mahasanghikas; Sthaviravada therefore belongs to the older Hinayana tradition and not to Mahayana, so statement 1 is wrong. The Lokottaravadins, who held that the Buddha was lokottara or transcendent, were an offshoot of the Mahasanghikas, so statement 2 is correct, and it was precisely this exaltation of the Buddha above ordinary humanity that supplied Mahayana with its transcendent Buddha and its Bodhisattva ideal, so statement 3 is correct.

answers.value: The Industrial Revolution ruined Indian handicrafts in the first half of the nineteenth century
answers.reasoning: Cheap machine-made British yarn and cloth flooded Indian markets in these decades while Indian manufactures faced prohibitive duties in Britain, and the result was the de-industrialisation that destroyed the livelihood of weavers and other artisans. The other options belong to a later period or are simply false: the first modern Indian textile mill was set up at Bombay only in 1854 and the first railway line ran in 1853, while colonial policy kept duties on British imports low rather than heavy.

answers.value: The correct order is 2 - 4 - 1 - 3: Mahendravarman I, then Gopala, then Bhoja, then Parantaka I
answers.reasoning: Mahendravarman I established Pallava power in the early seventh century, about 600 to 630. Gopala founded the Pala dynasty about 750. Mihira Bhoja, under whom the Gurjara-Pratiharas rose to their height, reigned in the ninth century, about 836 to 885. Parantaka I, who consolidated Chola power after Vijayalaya, ruled about 907 to 955. The sequence from earliest to latest is therefore 2, 4, 1, 3.

answers.value: A hundi was a bill of exchange
answers.reasoning: A hundi was a written instrument directing one party to pay a named sum to another - an indigenous bill of exchange by which merchants and bankers transferred money and extended credit over long distances without moving coin, and which could be endorsed and discounted. It was a commercial credit instrument, not a royal advisory, an account book or a feudal order.

answers.value: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; Deuskar's 'desh' meant the whole country, not Bengal alone
answers.reasoning: Desher Katha (1904) attacked colonial rule for more than its economic drain: it warned that the deeper conquest was of the Indian mind, which the colonial state had cast a spell over, so statement 1 holds. The book's extraordinary popularity fed straight into the swadeshi repertoire of street plays, jatra and folk song, so statement 2 holds. Statement 3 is what settles the option: Deuskar was a Marathi-descended writer working in Bengali, and his 'desh' was the whole country whose exploitation he documented, not the region of Bengal. Since statement 3 appears in every other option, only A survives.

answers.value: Vital-Vidhvansak was published by Gopal Baba Walangkar
answers.reasoning: Gopal Baba Walangkar, a retired army man of the Mahar community and an early follower of the Satyashodhak tradition, began Vital-Vidhvansak in 1888, and it is regarded as the first periodical addressed to untouchable readers. Phule's own journal was Deenbandhu, and Ambedkar's first paper, Mooknayak, appeared only in 1920, three decades later.

answers.value: Kulyavapa and dronavapa are units of land measurement
answers.reasoning: Kulyavapa, dronavapa and adhavapa occur in the Gupta-period copper-plate land grants of Bengal. Each expresses area indirectly, as the extent of land that a given measure of seed - a kulya, a drona - would sow, so the terms belong to land measurement and not to coinage, to categories of urban land or to ritual.

answers.value: The inscription is Ashoka's
answers.reasoning: The passage is from Ashoka's Rock Edict XII, on concord among religious sects. He urges restraint both in praising one's own sect and in disparaging others, warning that immoderate devotion injures the very sect it means to glorify. This plea for samavaya among sects is a hallmark of Ashoka's dhamma and is not associated with any of the other rulers named.

answers.value: Paramitas are the perfections whose attainment leads along the Bodhisattva path
answers.reasoning: In Mahayana thought the paramitas are the perfections a Bodhisattva cultivates - in the standard list of six, generosity, moral conduct, patience, energy, meditation and wisdom - and it is their perfection that carries him along the Bodhisattva path towards Buddhahood. The aphoristic law texts are the Dharmasutras, the schools rejecting Vedic authority are the nastika systems, and the great South Indian merchant guilds were the Ayyavole and the Manigramam.

answers.value: The Rakhmabai case involved all three - women's education, the age of consent, and restitution of conjugal rights
answers.reasoning: Rakhmabai, married as a child and then educated in her stepfather's household, refused to join her husband; Dadaji's suit of 1884 was in terms a suit for restitution of conjugal rights, which is statement 3 and the literal subject of the litigation. Because she had been married before she was old enough to consent, the case became the leading argument for raising the age of consent and fed directly into the Age of Consent Act of 1891, which is statement 2. Statement 1 is the judgement call: her schooling was itself part of the controversy, being blamed for her defiance, and her own letters to the press signed 'A Hindu Lady' pressed the case for educating girls instead of despatching them to their husbands. Option B, reading the case narrowly as consent plus restitution, is the runner-up. [Answer corrected to B from the official UPSC answer key; an independent blind derivation had reached D. The reasoning above argues for D and is retained so the disagreement is visible rather than hidden.]

answers.value: Indigo declined because synthetic dye made natural indigo unprofitable in the world market
answers.reasoning: Natural indigo was destroyed by chemistry rather than by politics. Adolf von Baeyer's synthesis of indigo was commercialised by BASF from 1897, and within a decade the cheap synthetic dye had swept the world market, leaving Indian plantations unable to compete. Peasant resistance had ended indigo in Bengal much earlier and only locally, and it cannot explain the collapse of the trade as a whole by the beginning of the twentieth century.

answers.value: Fort William College was founded to train British civil servants for administration in India
answers.reasoning: Wellesley set up Fort William College in 1800 because the young writers arriving from England reached India knowing nothing of its languages, laws or customs; the College taught them Persian, Arabic, Sanskrit and the vernaculars before they took up office. A revival of oriental learning and employment for scholars such as William Carey were by-products, not the purpose, and Wellesley acted on his own initiative - the Court of Directors in fact disapproved and reduced the institution.

answers.value: Ulgulan describes Birsa Munda's revolt of 1899-1900
answers.reasoning: Ulgulan, the Great Tumult, is the name given to the Munda rising led by Birsa Munda in Chotanagpur in 1899-1900 against the dikus, the landlords and the colonial revenue and forest system, in which Birsa also preached a new faith to his followers. The Revolt of 1857, the Mappila Rebellion and the Indigo Revolt are all known by other names.

answers.value: Only statement 3 is correct - Kalidasa is associated with Chandragupta II
answers.reasoning: Kalidasa is placed by tradition among the nine gems of the court of Chandragupta II Vikramaditya, so statement 3 is correct. Panini, the grammarian of the Ashtadhyayi, lived several centuries before the Shungas; the scholar linked with Pushyamitra Shunga is Patanjali, whose Mahabhashya is a commentary on Panini, so statement 1 confuses the two. Amarasimha, who compiled the Amarakosha, is likewise counted among Chandragupta II's gems and not among the literary men of Harshavardhana's court, who were Banabhatta and Mayura, so statement 2 is wrong.

answers.value: Pronuclear transfer is used to prevent mitochondrial diseases in offspring
answers.reasoning: Pronuclear transfer is a mitochondrial replacement technique. The mother's egg is fertilised, and the two pronuclei are then lifted out of the resulting zygote and placed in a donor zygote whose own pronuclei have been removed but whose mitochondria are healthy. The nuclear DNA remains the parents' and only the mitochondria are the donor's, so a mother carrying a mitochondrial disorder can avoid transmitting it to her child.

answers.value: Artificial Intelligence can do 1, 3 and 4 - cut industrial electricity use, diagnose disease and convert text to speech - but not transmit electrical energy wirelessly
answers.reasoning: Statement 5 settles the item: transmitting electrical energy without wires is a problem of physics and engineering - resonant inductive coupling, microwave or laser power beaming - and is not something an algorithm performs, so every option containing it falls and only B survives. Of the rest, AI schedules and optimises industrial and data-centre energy use (1), reads medical images and clinical data to support diagnosis (3), and drives modern text-to-speech systems (4). Statement 2 is defensible on its own terms, since generative models do produce stories and songs; the printed options offer no combination of 1, 2, 3 and 4, so the item only resolves if 'meaningful' is read strictly.

answers.value: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct; VLC is short-range, not long-range
answers.reasoning: Statement 2 decides the item and appears in every option except C: visible light communication depends on line of sight and on light that does not travel far, so it is a short-range optical wireless technology and calling it long-range is wrong. The others hold - VLC works in the visible band of roughly 375 to 780 nanometres (1), reaches data rates far above Bluetooth's (3), and because it carries data on light rather than on radio waves it neither causes nor suffers radio-frequency interference, which is why it can be used in hospitals, aircraft and other electromagnetically sensitive places (4).

answers.value: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; a blockchain is not limited to cryptocurrency data
answers.reasoning: A public blockchain is a shared, append-only ledger that any participant can inspect and verify and that no single party owns or administers, which is statement 1. It is permissionless in the further sense that anyone may build an application on it without seeking approval from an operator, which is statement 3. Statement 2 is wrong: the ledger is indifferent to what it records, and supply-chain events, land records, identity attestations and smart contracts all sit on blockchains - cryptocurrency is simply the first and best-known application.

answers.value: All four are correct - carbon nanotubes carry drugs and antigens, can form artificial capillaries, work in biochemical sensors, and are biodegradable
answers.reasoning: Nanotubes are studied as vehicles for delivering drugs and antigens into the body (1), and their conductivity and enormous surface-to-volume ratio make them sensitive transducers in biochemical sensors (3), so any option omitting these fails and only C and D remain. Statement 4 is not the older textbook position but is supported by the finding that nanotubes are degraded enzymatically, for instance by neutrophil myeloperoxidase, and both surviving options require it. Statement 2 is the judgement call - nanotube scaffolds have been explored as artificial capillaries and vascular grafts for injured tissue - and accepting it gives all four; rejecting it would give option C, the runner-up. [Answer corrected to C from the official UPSC answer key; an independent blind derivation had reached D. The reasoning above argues for D and is retained so the disagreement is visible rather than hidden.]

answers.value: Drones can do all three - spray pesticides, inspect volcanic craters, and collect whale breath samples
answers.reasoning: All three are done with current technology. Agricultural drones spray pesticide over crop fields and are in routine commercial use. Drones are flown over and into volcanic craters to sample gases and image vents where a crewed aircraft could not safely go. And drones of the SnotBot type hover in the blow of a surfacing whale to catch the exhaled spray, from which DNA, hormones and microbiota are analysed without ever touching the animal.

answers.value: The experiment is Evolved LISA (eLISA)
answers.reasoning: Three spacecraft flying in an equilateral formation with arms a million kilometres long and laser links between them is the design of the space-based gravitational-wave observatory in the LISA family, and the one-million-kilometre arm belongs to the Evolved LISA configuration. LISA Pathfinder was a single spacecraft flown only to test the instrument technology, so it cannot be the trio described, and Voyager-2 and New Horizons are single planetary probes.

answers.value: All three are correct - germline cells can be edited, an embryo's genome can be edited before birth, and human iPSCs can be injected into a pig embryo
answers.reasoning: All three are within reach of current technique. Editing can be directed at the germline cells that give rise to eggs and sperm, so that the change is heritable (1). An embryo's genome can be edited at the one-cell or early cleavage stage, which is what was done in the CRISPR-edited human embryos reported in 2018 (2). And human induced pluripotent stem cells have been injected into pig embryos to create human-pig chimaeras in research aimed at growing transplantable organs (3).

answers.value: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; the claim that the vaccines have no side effects is false
answers.reasoning: Streptococcus pneumoniae causes not only pneumonia but also meningitis, bacteraemia and sepsis, and the conjugate vaccine protects against the serotypes responsible for all of these, so statement 1 holds. Preventing the infection means the antibiotic is never needed, which cuts both antibiotic consumption and the selection pressure that breeds resistant strains, so statement 2 holds. Statement 3 is wrong on its face - no vaccine is free of side effects, and PCV commonly causes injection-site pain, swelling and fever and can rarely provoke allergic reactions.

answers.value: Public Key Infrastructure belongs to digital security infrastructure
answers.reasoning: Public Key Infrastructure is the framework of public and private key pairs, digital certificates, Certifying Authorities and the Controller of Certifying Authorities that underpins digital signatures and encrypted communication; in India it rests on the Information Technology Act, 2000. The term belongs to information security and has nothing to do with food, health, education, telecommunication or transport infrastructure.

answers.value: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; plant cells do have a plasma membrane, so statement 2 is false
answers.reasoning: Statement 2 is false and that alone fixes the answer: a plant cell has a plasma membrane exactly as an animal cell does, and the cellulose wall lies outside that membrane rather than replacing it. Statement 1 states the real difference, the wall of cellulose that animal cells lack. Statement 3 states the other standard difference - a mature plant cell is dominated by a single large central vacuole, whereas an animal cell has only small and scattered vacuoles and vesicles.

answers.value: All five are routes of benzene exposure
answers.reasoning: Benzene reaches people mainly by inhalation and all the listed routes carry it. It is a constituent of petrol and appears in vehicle exhaust (1); tobacco smoke is the largest single source of exposure for smokers and a major indoor source for others (2); the incomplete combustion of wood and other biomass releases it (3); and it occurs in the solvents of paints, lacquers, varnishes, glues and furniture wax, so freshly varnished furniture off-gasses it indoors (4). Statement 5 is the weakest link - benzene is a feedstock for plastics and resins, and polyurethane products can off-gas volatile organic compounds including benzene. Once statement 4 is accepted the printed options leave only 'all of the above', since options B and C omit statements that are certainly true; option A, which would follow if both 4 and 5 were rejected, is the runner-up. [Answer corrected to A from the official UPSC answer key; an independent blind derivation had reached D. The reasoning above argues for D and is retained so the disagreement is visible rather than hidden.]

answers.value: Only not depending on short-term foreign borrowings would give India immunity
answers.reasoning: Short-term foreign borrowing is the classic vulnerability in a crisis, because it must be rolled over at exactly the moment foreign lenders are withdrawing, so a country that has kept it small is far less exposed to a sudden stop - statement 1 is protective. The other two work the other way. Admitting more foreign banks multiplies the channels through which a shock abroad is transmitted to the domestic system, as a parent bank in difficulty pulls funds home. And full capital account convertibility removes precisely the friction that slows a stampede of capital out of the country; India's only partial convertibility was widely credited with insulating it in 2008.

answers.value: The aggregate money supply is left unchanged
answers.reasoning: Money supply on the M1 measure is currency held by the public plus demand deposits with banks plus other deposits with the Reserve Bank. Withdrawing cash simply moves rupees between the first two components: demand deposits fall by the amount withdrawn and currency with the public rises by exactly the same amount, so the total is unchanged and the immediate effect is nil. What does change is the banking system's reserves, which can affect the credit the banks create later - but that is a second-round effect, not the immediate one the question asks about.

answers.value: FDI is largely a non-debt creating capital inflow
answers.reasoning: The defining feature of Foreign Direct Investment is that the foreign investor takes an equity stake and shares in the enterprise's profits and losses; there is no fixed repayment obligation, so no external debt is created. This is why the RBI and the Economic Survey routinely describe FDI as the most stable, non-debt-creating component of the capital account. C is its opposite, since debt-servicing belongs to external commercial borrowings and other loan flows. A is wrong because FDI is made in both listed and unlisted companies, and investment through capital instruments in a listed company below the 10 per cent threshold is Foreign Portfolio Investment, not FDI. D describes FPI in government securities.

answers.value: West Texas Intermediate is a grade of crude oil
answers.reasoning: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) is a light, sweet crude oil produced in the United States and is one of the world's three main crude benchmarks, alongside Brent and Dubai/Oman. It is quoted on the NYMEX and is the pricing reference most often cited in news reports of oil prices. It has nothing to do with bullion, rare earths or uranium, none of which are graded under that name.

answers.value: All three — housing loans, credit card outstandings and Treasury bills are all borrowings of non-financial sectors
answers.reasoning: Non-financial debt is classified by who owes it, not by who holds it: it is the total debt of households, non-financial corporations and the government, as distinct from debt owed by banks and other financial intermediaries. Housing loans and credit card outstandings are household borrowings, so 1 and 2 qualify. Treasury bills are short-term borrowings of the Government of India, and government is a non-financial sector, so 3 qualifies as well. All three therefore belong to non-financial debt.

answers.value: Reactors running on imported uranium are placed under safeguards; those on domestic fuel are not
answers.reasoning: Under the 2006 Separation Plan that flowed from the India–US civil nuclear agreement, India separated its civilian and strategic nuclear facilities and offered the civilian ones for IAEA safeguards. The practical dividing line is fuel: reactors fuelled with imported uranium, and the imported fuel itself, must be under safeguards so that the supplier can verify it is not diverted to weapons use, whereas reactors run on indigenous uranium remain outside safeguards. Raising the MSF rate (2) makes emergency overnight borrowing from the RBI dearer and tightens liquidity, which is contractionary and therefore the one action an expansionist RBI would avoid. Computerising Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (2) builds institutional infrastructure, social capital development (3) builds durable institutional capacity, and setting up cold storages (6) creates physical assets — all investment. Fixing the Minimum Support Price (1) is a price-support instrument, free electricity (4) is an input subsidy, and loan waivers (5) are a fiscal transfer; none of the three creates an asset, and in the Economic Survey's own framing they are precisely the revenue-side subsidies that crowd out public investment in agriculture.

answers.value: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; statement 3 inverts the ratio's meaning

A bank uses it both to gauge a borrower's present repayment capacity (1) and, by tracking its trend, to spot deteriorating or emerging risk before default (2). Statement 3 reverses the relationship: a higher ratio means a larger earnings cushion over interest and therefore a better, not worse, ability to service debt.

answers.value: All four — MSP, government trading, government stockpiling and consumer subsidies have all influenced rice prices

answers.value: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct — Parivrajaka is a wandering renunciant and Upasaka is a Buddhist lay follower

Manas is associated with the pygmy hog and hispid hare, Mudumalai with elephants and tigers, and Tal Chhapar with blackbuck.

answers.value: All three — steel slag is used in road bases, as an agricultural soil amendment and in cement manufacture
answers.reasoning: Steel slag is a hard, dense, angular by-product of steelmaking, which makes it an excellent aggregate for road sub-base and base courses (1). Being rich in calcium and silicon and alkaline in reaction, it is used as a liming agent and silicate fertiliser to correct acid soils and supply micronutrients (2). Granulated slag has latent hydraulic properties and is blended into Portland slag cement, which is why steel plants supply it to cement makers (3). All three uses are established, so D.

Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary (3) is a lowland terai forest of the Dudhwa landscape in Uttar Pradesh, and Manas (4) is a Brahmaputra floodplain and foothill park in Assam; neither reaches the altitude musk deer need.

answers.value: Copper slag, cold mix asphalt technology and geotextiles are the environmentally preferred choices
answers.reasoning: Copper slag (1) is an industrial waste reused as aggregate, avoiding fresh quarrying. Cold mix technology (2) uses bitumen emulsion at ambient temperature and so avoids the heating of aggregate and binder, cutting fuel use and emissions sharply — it is promoted under PMGSY for exactly this reason. Geotextiles (3) strengthen weak subgrades and reduce the thickness of aggregate needed. Hot mix asphalt (4) is the energy-intensive alternative that cold mix is meant to replace, and Portland cement (5) is one of the most carbon-intensive materials in construction. Hence 1, 2 and 3 only.

answers.value: All three statements are correct
answers.reasoning: Coal ash concentrates the trace elements present in coal, including arsenic, lead and mercury, which is why fly ash ponds are a heavy-metal leaching hazard (1). Burning coal oxidises its sulphur and atmospheric nitrogen, releasing sulphur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen, the precursors of acid rain (2). Indian coal is of Gondwana origin, formed by drift deposition, and characteristically has high ash content of about 30 to 45 per cent with low sulphur (3). All three are correct.

answers.value: All three — biochar serves as a growing medium in vertical farming, supports nitrogen-fixing microbes and improves water retention
answers.reasoning: Biochar is a porous charcoal-like material made by pyrolysis of biomass. Its porosity and low bulk density make it a component of soilless and vertical-farming growing media (1), and that same pore structure holds water against drainage, extending the medium's water-retention time (3). Statement 2 is the judgement call: biochar's pores provide refuge and habitat for soil microbes and it raises pH and supplies micronutrients such as molybdenum and boron, and field trials report enhanced biological nitrogen fixation by rhizobia in biochar-amended media, so it is accepted as correct. Runner-up C, which takes 1 and 3 only, follows if statement 2 is treated as an over-claim.

answers.value: A licence or prior permission is needed to cultivate a Schedule VI plant
answers.reasoning: Schedule VI was inserted into the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 by the 1991 amendment and lists specified plants such as the blue vanda, ladies' slipper orchid, pitcher plant, red vanda, beddomes' cycad and kuth. Section 17A prohibits picking, uprooting, possessing, selling or transporting them, but Section 17B and the licensing provisions expressly allow cultivation with the prior permission of the Chief Wild Life Warden. So cultivation is regulated, not forbidden, which rules out B. C is wrong because Schedule VI has nothing to do with genetic modification, and D is wrong because the schedule protects threatened native plants, the opposite of invasive species.

Their common thread is location on the sea and a commercial rather than political or religious identity, which rules out capitals, art centres and pilgrimage sites.

answers.value: All three are advantages of zero tillage
answers.reasoning: Zero tillage sows directly into undisturbed soil through the previous crop's residue, so wheat can be drilled into standing paddy stubble without burning it — the principle behind the Happy Seeder (1). It also underlies direct seeded rice, in which paddy seed is sown straight into the field, dispensing with the nursery and transplanting of seedlings (2). Because the soil is not inverted, organic matter is not oxidised and residue is retained on the surface, so soil organic carbon builds up, giving carbon sequestration (3). Note also that statements 1 and 3 are plainly correct and no option offers those two alone, which independently confirms D.

answers.value: Cassava, damaged wheat grains, rotten potatoes and sugar beet — 1, 2, 5 and 6

Groundnut seeds (3) and horse gram (4) are edible foodstuffs and are not in the notified list — the policy's whole design is to use surplus, damaged or non-food material rather than divert edible produce. Hence 1, 2, 5 and 6 only.

answers.value: The monetary value of the long-term damage done by one tonne of carbon dioxide emitted in a given year
answers.reasoning: The Social Cost of Carbon is defined as the present value, in money terms, of the total future damages caused by emitting one additional tonne of carbon dioxide in a particular year — covering losses from changed agricultural yields, health effects, property damage from flooding and so on. It is used to price the externality of emissions in policy cost-benefit analysis. B describes fossil fuel dependence, C describes climate adaptation by a displaced person, and D describes an individual carbon footprint; none of them is a damage-cost measure per tonne.

answers.value: Only statement 1 is correct — black gram is grown in both kharif and rabi seasons
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: black gram (urad) is a kharif crop in northern and central India and is also grown as a rabi and summer crop in the south and in rice-fallow areas, so it spans both seasons. answers.value: Cotton
answers.reasoning: The description is the standard set of cotton's climatic requirements: it is a subtropical crop, hard frost kills it, it needs at least 210 frost-free days, 50 to 100 centimetres of rainfall, and a light, well-drained but moisture-retentive soil — the black cotton and alluvial soils of India. Jute is ruled out because it needs a hot humid climate with 150 to 200 centimetres of rainfall and grows on new alluvium. Sugarcane needs a longer growing period, heavier soils and 75 to 150 centimetres of rain. Tea needs 150 to 250 centimetres of well-distributed rainfall on sloping land, far above the range given.

answers.value: Neither statement is correct — solar power runs submersible pumps and piston pumps as well
answers.reasoning: Both statements assert a restriction that does not exist. Solar photovoltaic power drives a motor, and the motor is indifferent to where the pump sits, so solar submersible pumps for deep borewells are standard equipment under the PM-KUSUM programme, refuting statement 1. Likewise solar power runs positive-displacement pumps, including piston and diaphragm types, which are in fact preferred for low-discharge, high-head applications because they work well at the variable power a solar array delivers; that refutes statement 2. Hence neither.

answers.value: Statements 1 and 4 are correct — bud chip settlings save seed material, and tissue-cultured settlings can be used
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: the bud chip method scoops out only the bud with a small piece of surrounding tissue and raises it in a nursery, cutting seed cane requirement from several tonnes per hectare to a fraction of it. Statement 4 is correct: tissue-culture raised settlings are a recognised route to disease-free, genetically uniform planting material. Statements 2 and 3 are both wrong and for the same underlying reason — a sett with more buds carries larger food reserves in its internodes, so multi-budded setts give better germination and better survival under adverse weather than single-budded setts, not worse.

answers.value: Crop diversification, legume intensification and tensiometer use — vertical farming is not counted
answers.reasoning: Crop diversification (1) breaks monoculture, reduces pest pressure and eases the water demand of paddy-wheat rotations. Legume intensification (2) fixes atmospheric nitrogen biologically and cuts urea use. The tensiometer (3) measures soil moisture tension so that irrigation is applied only when the soil needs it, and it is promoted in Punjab precisely to save groundwater. All three are recognised eco-friendly practices in Indian agriculture. Vertical farming (4) is a controlled-environment production technology that is land- and water-efficient but heavily dependent on artificial lighting and climate control, and it is not an established eco-friendly agricultural practice in the Indian context. Runner-up D, if vertical farming is credited on its water and land savings alone.

answers.value: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct; rock phosphate cannot be applied through fertigation
answers.reasoning: Fertigation delivers dissolved nutrients through the irrigation water. Acids can be injected along with the fertiliser to neutralise bicarbonates and control the alkalinity of the irrigation water, which is routine practice in drip systems (1). Nutrients reach the root zone in solution and in small frequent doses, raising their availability to the plant (3) and reducing losses below the root zone through leaching (4). Statement 2 is wrong: rock phosphate is virtually insoluble in water and would clog emitters, and phosphatic fertilisers in general are difficult in fertigation because phosphate precipitates with the calcium and magnesium in irrigation water — only highly soluble forms such as phosphoric acid or mono-ammonium phosphate can be used, so the claim that 'all other phosphatic fertilizers' can be efficiently applied fails.

answers.value: Chromite, kyanite and sillimanite are major minerals; bentonite has been declared a minor mineral
answers.reasoning: Under the MMDR Act the Centre lists minor minerals, and everything not so listed is a major mineral. Kyanite and sillimanite are refractory raw materials reported in the Indian Bureau of Mines' major mineral statistics, so 3 and 4 also qualify. Bentonite (1) was among the minerals notified as minor minerals in 2015, alongside items such as brick earth, fuller's earth, marble and ordinary sand, and so falls outside the major category. The pivot in this item is the classification of bentonite; option A follows only if bentonite is still treated as major.

answers.value: Both statements are correct

Statement 2 is correct because that is the entire purpose of the index: OMT integrates heat over the whole column rather than just the skin, so it is a more stable predictor than sea surface temperature, and Indian researchers have shown that the January to March OMT in this region correlates with whether the following monsoon's rainfall will be above or below the long-period average. The specific 129-metre figure is what makes this an item of recall rather than reasoning, hence the moderate confidence. [Answer corrected to B from the official UPSC answer key; an independent blind derivation had reached C. The reasoning above argues for C and is retained so the disagreement is visible rather than hidden.]

answers.value: Statements 2 and 3 are correct; fertilizer retail prices are not fully market-driven

Statement 3 is correct: elemental sulphur, used to make the sulphuric acid that digests rock phosphate into phosphoric acid, is recovered as a by-product of desulphurising crude oil at refineries.

answers.value: Only statement 2 is correct — some cyclones develop an eye, and the eye is warmer, not cooler

Statement 2 is correct: a clear eye forms only in intense, well-organised tropical cyclones; weaker tropical storms and all temperate cyclones lack one. Statement 3 is wrong and is the reverse of the truth: air subsiding in the eye is compressed and warms adiabatically, so a tropical cyclone has a warm core and the eye is several degrees warmer than its surroundings, not about ten degrees cooler.

answers.value: Nagarjunsagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve has the largest Critical Tiger Habitat
answers.reasoning: Nagarjunsagar-Srisailam, spread across Andhra Pradesh and Telangana in the Nallamala hills, is India's largest tiger reserve, and its notified Critical Tiger Habitat runs to roughly 2,600 square kilometres. That is well ahead of the Sundarbans at about 1,700, Ranthambore at about 1,100 and Corbett at about 820 square kilometres. Size of the reserve as a whole is the useful cue here, and Nagarjunsagar-Srisailam is by a wide margin the largest of the four.
